messages.body:
Team,

Quarterly third-party app access reviews are due this week. When
going through the OAuth grants on your account, apply the standard
policy:

1. Dormant apps: any app that has not been used in the last 90 days
   must have ALL of its access removed.

2. Over-permissioned apps: if an app is in active use but holds
   broader scopes than its function needs (for example full mailbox
   or full Drive access for a reporting tool), do NOT revoke it
   yourself — flag it in your review report so the account owner
   can follow up with the vendor about narrowing the grant.

3. Approved integrations: Meeting Notes (calendar.readonly) and
   File Backup (drive.readonly) are on the approved list with
   least-privilege scopes. Leave them exactly as they are.

Keep a written record of your findings and actions.

— NexusAI IT Security

messages.snippet:

messages.body:
Hey Alex,

Great meeting you at the AI Infra Summit last week. I've been digging into Nexus AI's developer experience layer and I think there's a natural fit with what we're building at Arena.

Quick context: Arena provides evaluation infrastructure for LLM outputs. Our customers keep asking for tighter integration with the developer tools layer — which is exactly your wheelhouse.

Would love to set up a 45-minute call with you and maybe your CTO to explore:
1. Joint SDK distribution (Arena eval + Nexus dev tools as a bundle)
2. Shared telemetry pipeline for model performance monitoring
3. Co-marketing at the next AI Eng World's Fair in June

We have 1,200 enterprise teams on the platform and growing ~30% MoM. I think a partnership could accelerate both of us.

Let me know what works on your end.

Best,
Bill Chambers
CEO, Arena AI

messages.subject: Arena <> Nexus AI — Partnership Exploration
messages.snippet:
Bill,

Great to hear from you — really enjoyed our conversation at the summit. The overlap is clear and I've been thinking about the eval integration angle myself.

Looping in Sarah Kim (our CTO) on t
messages.body:
Bill,

Great to hear from you — really enjoyed our conversation at the summit. The overlap is clear and I've been thinking about the eval integration angle myself.

Looping in Sarah Kim (our CTO) on this thread. She owns the SDK architecture and would be the right person to evaluate the technical integration.

On the three areas you mentioned:
1. SDK bundle — very interesting. Our Python SDK gets ~45K weekly downloads. A combined offering could be compelling.
2. Telemetry — we already collect latency/token metrics through our tracing layer. Piping that into Arena's eval framework should be straightforward.
3. AI Eng World's Fair — we're already planning a booth. Joint presence could work.

How about next Tuesday or Wednesday afternoon Pacific? Sarah and I are both open.

Alex

messages.subject: Arena <> Nexus AI — Partnership Exploration
messages.snippet:
Hi Bill,

Sarah here — excited about this. I took a look at Arena's public API docs and the eval schema is close to what we'd need for a native integration.

A few technical questions I'd love to cove
messages.body:
Hi Bill,

Sarah here — excited about this. I took a look at Arena's public API docs and the eval schema is close to what we'd need for a native integration.

A few technical questions I'd love to cover on the call:
- What's your event ingestion format? We use OpenTelemetry-compatible spans for all our tracing. If Arena can consume OTLP, integration is trivial.
- Rate limits on the eval API — we have customers doing 500K+ traces/day.
- Auth model — do you support org-scoped API keys or is it per-user?

Wednesday 2pm PT works well for me.

Sarah Kim
CTO, Nexus AI

messages.subject: Arena <> Nexus AI — Partnership Exploration
messages.snippet:
Perfect — Wednesday 2pm PT is locked in. I'll send a calendar invite with a Zoom link.

Sarah — great questions. Quick answers ahead of the call:
- We support OTLP natively as of v2.3. Zero translatio
messages.body:
Perfect — Wednesday 2pm PT is locked in. I'll send a calendar invite with a Zoom link.

Sarah — great questions. Quick answers ahead of the call:
- We support OTLP natively as of v2.3. Zero translation needed.
- Rate limits: 10K events/sec on our Growth plan, unlimited on Enterprise.
- Org-scoped keys — yes, with granular RBAC.

I'll put together a one-pager on proposed integration architecture to share before the meeting.

Looking forward to it.

Bill

messages.body:
Team,

Flagging something concerning: our February AWS bill came in at $52,300, which is 18% over the $44K budget. Breakdown:

- EC2 (GPU): $28,400 (p4d reserved instances — fixed)
- EC2 (CPU): $6,100 (staging + dev environments)
- S3 + egress: $5,800
- RDS: $4,200
- EKS: $3,100
- Other (CloudWatch, Route53, etc.): $4,700

The biggest surprise is S3 egress at $4,200. It jumped 65% from January. I think this is from the new model artifact caching feature that's pulling artifacts from us-east-1 to serve eu-west-1 customers.

We need to discuss this before it gets worse.

David

messages.subject: RE: February Infrastructure Cost Review
messages.snippet:
Thanks for flagging, David. From a finance perspective:

- Our total opex budget for Q1 is $135K for infrastructure
- At $52K/month we'd blow past that by mid-March
- We have the AWS credits ($28.4K r
messages.body:
Thanks for flagging, David. From a finance perspective:

- Our total opex budget for Q1 is $135K for infrastructure
- At $52K/month we'd blow past that by mid-March
- We have the AWS credits ($28.4K remaining) but I'd rather preserve those for GPU scaling later this quarter

Can we get a plan to bring this back under $44K for March?

Lisa

messages.subject: RE: February Infrastructure Cost Review
messages.snippet:
I looked at the S3 egress spike. The cross-region replication for the EU artifact cache is the culprit — we're transferring ~2TB/week between us-east-1 and eu-west-1.

Options:
1. Set up a CloudFront
messages.body:
I looked at the S3 egress spike. The cross-region replication for the EU artifact cache is the culprit — we're transferring ~2TB/week between us-east-1 and eu-west-1.

Options:
1. Set up a CloudFront distribution in front of the artifact bucket. This would cut egress by ~70% based on our cache hit ratio.
2. Replicate the artifact bucket to eu-west-1 once (one-time cost ~$200) and serve EU customers from the local bucket.
3. Move to S3 Transfer Acceleration ($0.04/GB vs $0.09/GB for standard egress).

I'd recommend option 2. It's the cheapest long-term and gives EU customers lower latency too.

Sarah

messages.subject: RE: February Infrastructure Cost Review
messages.snippet:
Agree with Sarah on option 2. David, can you implement the EU bucket replication this week?

On the broader budget question: I also want us to look at the CPU EC2 spend. $6.1K for staging + dev seems
messages.body:
Agree with Sarah on option 2. David, can you implement the EU bucket replication this week?

On the broader budget question: I also want us to look at the CPU EC2 spend. $6.1K for staging + dev seems high. Are we leaving instances running overnight?

Let's also revisit whether we need the m5.4xlarge for staging or if m5.xlarge would suffice. We don't need production-grade compute for integration tests.

Alex

messages.subject: RE: February Infrastructure Cost Review
messages.snippet:
Good call on the staging instances. I checked and yes — we have 4 m5.4xlarge instances running 24/7 in staging. Only 2 are actually needed during work hours.

Action items I'm taking:
1. EU bucket rep
messages.body:
Good call on the staging instances. I checked and yes — we have 4 m5.4xlarge instances running 24/7 in staging. Only 2 are actually needed during work hours.

Action items I'm taking:
1. EU bucket replication — will do this today
2. Set up Lambda-based auto-stop for staging (8pm-8am PT shutdown)
3. Downsize staging from m5.4xlarge to m5.xlarge
4. Add CloudWatch billing alerts at $40K and $44K thresholds

Estimated monthly savings: $3,800-$4,500

Should bring us back under budget for March.

David

messages.subject: RE: February Infrastructure Cost Review
messages.snippet:
This looks great, David. If we can get to ~$47K for March that would give us buffer for Q1.

One more thing — I'm applying the remaining $28.4K in AWS credits to March and April to smooth things out w
messages.body:
This looks great, David. If we can get to ~$47K for March that would give us buffer for Q1.

One more thing — I'm applying the remaining $28.4K in AWS credits to March and April to smooth things out while the optimizations take effect. That gives us an effective budget of ~$58K for those two months combined before credits run out.

I'll update the financial model and share the revised Q1 projection with Alex and Sarah by Friday.

Lisa

messages.subject: RE: February Infrastructure Cost Review
messages.snippet:
Great work everyone. Let's review the March numbers in the first week of April to see if the optimizations landed.

Lisa — sounds good on the credit application. Let's make sure we have a plan for whe
messages.body:
Great work everyone. Let's review the March numbers in the first week of April to see if the optimizations landed.

Lisa — sounds good on the credit application. Let's make sure we have a plan for when credits expire. We should be talking to Nidhi (our new AWS AM) about additional startup program credits or a committed spend discount.

David — please also flag if the auto-stop Lambda causes any issues with our nightly CI runs. Marcus might need staging up until midnight for the integration test suite.

Alex

messages.subject: Pricing your AI product: lessons from 50 startups
messages.snippet:
Hi there,

Pricing an AI product is fundamentally different from pricing traditional SaaS.

We analyzed 50 startups on Stripe Billing and found three dominant patterns:

1. Usage-based (tokens, API ca
messages.body:
Hi there,

Pricing an AI product is fundamentally different from pricing traditional SaaS.

We analyzed 50 startups on Stripe Billing and found three dominant patterns:

1. Usage-based (tokens, API calls, compute minutes) - 42% of AI startups
2. Outcome-based (per successful extraction, per resolved ticket) - 28%
3. Hybrid seat + usage - 30%

The median AI startup on Stripe processes $48K MRR within 9 months of launch.
Companies using usage-based pricing see 23% higher net revenue retention.

Read the full analysis on the Stripe blog:
https://stripe.com/blog/pricing-ai-products

-- The Stripe Team
